description.value: The study investigated brain activation, heart rate variability, and their coupling during paced breathing, psychosocial stress induction, and stress recovery in healthy adults.

spans.text: During MRI-scanning, participants performed a paced-breathing and stress induction task.

To assess the association between HRV and brain activation, we adopted a sliding window approach 46 in STATA, where both IBI and RMSSD time-series were resampled at the fMRI TR and subsequently mean-centered.

design.value: A within-subject, single-session fMRI study using a block-design paced-breathing and Montreal Imaging Stress Task paradigm, with continuous physiological recording and repeated-measures and brain–heart association analyses.

spans.text: Each participant underwent a single MRI-scanning session.

The task begins with 4 min of normal breathing, where participants are free to breathe at their own pace (“unpaced breathing”). Following this, participants are instructed via a visual cue to breathe at a normal rate of 10 breaths/min for 4 min (“normal paced breathing”).
Subsequently, a general linear model was constructed employing a block-design, where the different events during the task were modeled using boxcar functions.

steps.value: Exclusion of first four volumes; slice time correction; realignment and unwarping; coregistration of T1 images with mean T2* images; normalization to MNI space; smoothing with an 8 mm Gaussian kernel.

spans.text: The following pre-processing steps were used: Exclusion of first four volumes to account for magnetic field for equilibration, slice time correction, realignment and unwarping to correct for artifacts due to susceptibility-by-movement interactions, coregistration of T1 images with the mean T2* images, normalization to MNI space (functional: 3mm3, anatomical: 1mm3), smoothing of functional images (8 mm Gaussian kernel).
The resulting time-series were then used as a regressor in the general linear model (GLM) fMRI analysis
